pixel_convention: x to the right, y DOWN, origin at top-left pixel centre; all values in pixels and seconds

camera.evidence: phase correlation vs frame 0 over all 300 frames: max shift 0.006 px (upper image) and 0.031 px (lower-right); no zoom
camera.perspective_note: Labelled 2D, but the render is a real 3D kitchen seen nearly front-on. The apple's path is roughly in one plane; its apparent diameter stays constant (fit radius 30.5 -> 30.0 px, box 62-63 x 64-65 px) through the whole clip, so one pixel scale for the whole trajectory is appropriate.

objects.name: apple
objects.distinguish: the ONLY moving object; red-orange apple/peach, ~62 px across, starts at left end of the kitchen island/counter at (689,1072), left of the static peach pair on the plate
objects.reference_point: ref_x, ref_y = centre of a circle fitted to the apple outline (= rigid-body centre / origin)

size_px.note: mask includes 1-2 px anti-aliased rim; apple is slightly lumpy, so width/height wobble +/-2 px as it rotates

phases.what: rolls left along the counter top, accelerating from rest; centre drops slowly from y 1072 to ~1104 (counter/board slopes toward camera-left), x 689 -> 369; about -3.7 px/frame horizontally by frames 120-141
rolls off the counter's left edge (~x 352-370) and falls in a projectile arc to the floor; horizontal ~ -3.7 px/frame stays nearly constant, vertical increases ~0.42 px/frame per frame
impact on the floor (lowest centre y 1744.3 at frame 192; contact between frames 191 and 192)
small bounce: apex y ~1734.5 at frames 198-200 (~10 px above impact), lands again ~frame 204-205
rolls left on the floor at centre y ~1740-1745, ~ -2.0 to -2.5 px/frame, exits the left image edge (cut from frame 263, gone after frame 288)
